_comment: Start-up thresholds (scripts/ci/startup-bench.mjs, scripts/bench/busy-host.mjs). Measured 2026-11-16/17 on the Mac mini: 22 invocations of 5 starts (110 starts) of the debug .app: unstressed, under yes/dd stress, and 3 invocations at a host load of 140 to 177 and 0% CPU idle (other agents' builds); results block 'Start-up benchmark on a busy host' in apps/debrief/docs/performance.md. Rule (user, 2026-11-17): the benchmark is always taken and never refused for a busy host; it fails only on a real regression. cpu: ms of CPU (user + sys) of the app's process tree at firstInteractive. FAILS over baselineMs + noiseMs. baselineMs = median of the 22 invocation medians (515). noiseMs 360 makes the threshold 875 = 1.25 times the worst invocation median measured (700, at load 150 and 0% idle): CPU time did not move under yes/dd loops (480 to 540) but rose to 530 to 720 under real build load, so a tighter threshold would fail on a busy host. A start-up that needs 70% more CPU than idle is a regression. marks: ms since the process start. Over baselineMs + noiseMs (baseline = median of the 22 invocation medians, noise = 3 standard deviations of them) is only a NOTE: wall time moves with host load (up to 2.5 times its baseline for a single start at load 150). A mark FAILS only over wallCeilingFactor times its baseline. wallCeilingFactor 5: the worst single start of the 110 was 2.52 times its mark's baseline (setupDone), so 5 is twice that, and a broken start is far beyond it (the app waits 10 s for a first paint before it gives up, 16 times the firstInteractive baseline). reference: the fixed workload's best idle time; the ratio to it is a note only (it slows 2 to 5 times under the loads that leave the start unmoved). Linux reports only until its first nightly numbers are recorded here.
